name: Qwen Image 2.1 — reshoot from another angle (multiple angles)
description:
Reshoot the same subject from a different camera position. Upload one photo, pick an angle and a height, and Qwen-Image-2.1 with a camera-control adapter renders that subject as seen from there — the back of an object really is its back, not a mirrored front.

★ The prompt is BUILT FOR YOU from the two dropdowns. The adapter answers only to its own grammar, which starts with the trigger word <mva>, and a prompt missing it produces a perfectly plausible picture with the camera never having moved — so the trigger is wired into the graph as a fixed literal instead of being something to remember. 12 angles × 8 heights (each with a close-up variant) = 96 framings, and every one is the documented spelling.

★ To build a turnaround, schedule it once per angle on the same photo and the same seed — the dropdown is in turning order, so working down it walks the camera around the subject.

★ 'Adapter version' switches between the author's two releases on the same picture and seed: **v2 (step 1500, rank 64)** is the recommended one and was trained with characters and full-precision weights; **v1 (step 1000, rank 32)** is the original, kept for comparison. Strength 0.8–1.0 — start at 1.0, and if the result drifts back toward simply copying your photo, lower it to 0.8 rather than switching version.

⚠ It was trained on 512×512 renders, so your photo is scaled to about that before it is used, and the result comes back that size. Raising 'Reference size' is outside what the adapter saw — the card says larger canvases inherit the style but were not trained on.

⚠ It was trained on rendered objects. Real photos do work — the author shows a dog, a cat and an apple — but fine detail like fur softens, and a turn is a re-render, so anything the original photo could not see is invented. Experimental: not used in a class yet.

Licence: the adapter is Apache 2.0, unusually permissive for this family — but the Qwen-Image-2.1 base it runs on is Qwen Research, research and evaluation only, so the combination is not for commercial work.

promptGuides.label: The adapter’s own model card (pose dictionary, examples, honest limits)
promptGuides.tip: There is nothing to write: the two dropdowns are the whole prompt grammar, and the <mva> trigger is built into the graph. The card shows what each angle looks like on real photos.

author: Template - ComfyUI

models.note: Camera-control LoRA, v2 step 1500, rank 64, trained on Qwen-Image-2.1 at 512². Trigger '<mva>'. Renamed on download from the repo's 80-character checkpoint filename. 192 of 192 modules map onto this rig's fused int8-convrot build.
The v1 release, step 1000, rank 32. Kept so the two can be compared on one picture and seed; the author recommends v2.

exposedParameters.label: The subject to reshoot — one clear photo, the subject filling the frame
Camera angle — where the camera stands, going round the subject
Camera height and framing — eye level, raised, high, or straight down
Adapter version (v2 is the author’s recommendation)
Adapter strength (0.8–1.0; lower it if the camera will not move)
Reference size in megapixels — 0.26 is the 512² it was trained at, and also the size of the result
Steps (40 is the author’s own setting)
Seed — keep it fixed across angles to build a consistent turnaround
